Formulation  
A 26-year-old female teacher presents with work-related stress manifesting alongside a new onset itchy, dry, and red rash predominantly affecting hands and arms after recent swimming exposure. No prior skin conditions; symptoms may be precipitated by environmental triggers (swimming pool exposure, possible irritants) with perpetuation due to ongoing stress and skin dryness. Family history includes atopy (asthma, hay fever), suggesting possible atopic predisposition. Protective factors include absence of substance use and social isolation. Management targets stress reduction and topical treatment of suspected dermatitis.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Work-related stress  
- Patient Goal(s): To reduce perceived stress and improve ability to cope with work demands  
- Clinical Goal(s): Identify and implement stress management strategies; monitor impact on skin and general wellbeing  
- Actions (Patient): Engage in stress reduction techniques; report any worsening symptoms or mood changes  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide support and advice regarding stress; consider referral to counseling or mental health services if stress persists or worsens  

Secondary Problem: Dermatitis  
- Patient Goal(s): Resolution of itchy, dry, red rash on hands and arms  
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce skin inflammation and dryness; relieve itch  
- Actions (Patient): Apply prescribed steroid creams and emollients as instructed; consider over-the-counter antihistamines for itch  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide steroid cream prescription and emollient advice; offer patient information leaflet on dermatitis; advise on avoidance of irritants; arrange follow-up if no improvement in 1 week  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes  
- Topics Covered: Dermatitis causes and management; use of topical steroids and emollients; over-the-counter antihistamines; impact of stress on skin  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistence or worsening of rash, spreading, development of cracking or infection, increased itchiness unresponsive to treatment  
- Coping Strategies: Stress management techniques advised informally; consideration of formal counseling if needed
